summary: Content-only verification: crawled 10 public pages (Home, About, Products, a product detail, GlobalReach, Gallery, Updates list, Catalogs, Contact, Quote) + /certificates + all 3 Updates detail pages via headless browser and inspected visible innerText, <title>, and <meta name=description>. Result: 'Dubai' is fully removed from all static React source and from every page's title/meta and body EXCEPT two Updates detail pages whose content is served from MongoDB seeded data (backend/seed.py lines 27 and 43). Regression checks pass: hero reads 'exported worldwide.', About shows both directors with photos loading (Muhammad Ali Piracha 325x767, Sultan Ali Piracha 328x587), footer shows 'Business Centre, Sharjah Publishing City Free Zone, Sharjah, United Arab Emirates', copyright '© 2026 NBMT Trading Co., United Arab Emirates', Certificates nav link is gone, /certificates route renders no certificates content. No blocking console errors (only expected 401 on /api/auth/me for unauthenticated users).

minor.issue: MongoDB updates collection still contains 'Dubai' in the body of two seeded updates ('new-season-basmati-rice-now-available-for-export' and 'nbmt-trading-co-welcomes-new-buyers-across-the-gulf'). These render on the public Updates detail pages. Source: /app/backend/seed.py lines 27 ("shipment from Dubai on FOB and CIF terms") and 43 ("independent Dubai trading house" + "With our base in Dubai and access to Jebel Ali").

ui_bugs.issue: Displays 'Dubai' in body copy for 2 of 3 seeded updates (data-driven, comes from MongoDB, not from React source)

action_items: Update /app/backend/seed.py — replace 'Dubai' with 'UAE'/'the UAE' in the two update bodies (lines 27 and 43).

Update the two existing update documents in MongoDB (by slug 'new-season-basmati-rice-now-available-for-export' and 'nbmt-trading-co-welcomes-new-buyers-across-the-gulf') so the change takes effect on the live site — rerunning seed.py alone will NOT overwrite existing docs unless the seeder is idempotent on update. A direct db.updates.update_many or a small one-off script is required.
critical_code_review_comments: Seed data in /app/backend/seed.py was not updated as part of the 'remove Dubai' content change, causing a divergence between React source (clean) and DB-served content (still contains Dubai). Any future global text changes should include a grep sweep of backend seed files and a corresponding DB migration/update step.
Consider making seed.py idempotent-with-update (upsert by slug) or add a lightweight migration script so content edits ship consistently.

success_rate.frontend: 10/12 pages clean (83%); 2 Updates detail pages contain Dubai from DB seed

seed_data_creation: None. Existing MongoDB seed data was inspected only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The only remaining Dubai occurrences are in MongoDB-stored update bodies (not in React source). After main agent fixes seed.py AND updates the existing 2 update docs in Mongo, re-verify by curl-ing /api/updates and by visiting /updates/new-season-basmati-rice-now-available-for-export and /updates/nbmt-trading-co-welcomes-new-buyers-across-the-gulf. Base URL: https://global-grains-3.preview.emergentagent.com. Grep in browser: page.evaluate("() => (document.body.innerText.match(/dubai/gi)||[]).length").
rca of the issue: Reproduction: (1) curl https://global-grains-3.preview.emergentagent.com/api/updates — response bodies contain 'Dubai' in 2 of 3 updates. (2) Visit /updates/new-season-basmati-rice-now-available-for-export — visible text contains 'shipment from Dubai on FOB and CIF terms'. (3) Visit /updates/nbmt-trading-co-welcomes-new-buyers-across-the-gulf — visible text contains 'independent Dubai trading house' and 'With our base in Dubai and access to Jebel Ali'. Root cause: The 'remove Dubai' content pass updated the React source but missed /app/backend/seed.py, and even after fixing seed.py the two update documents already exist in MongoDB and will not be overwritten by a re-run of seed.py (unless it upserts). Mitigation: (a) edit seed.py lines 27 and 43 to replace 'Dubai' with 'the UAE'/'UAE'; (b) run a one-off db.updates.update_one({slug: ...}, {$set: {body: ...}}) for each of the two documents, or drop-and-reseed the updates collection.
